prompt: Where does the name Extreme Programming come from?

choices.text: Working extremely long hours to meet each deadline the customer sets
choices.why: XP argues for a sustainable pace.

choices.text: Very large teams
Taking good practices as far as they go
choices.why: Right: if reviewing is good, review all the time.

choices.text: A team at Chrysler that practised extreme sports between releases

prompt: Match each XP practice to what it does for testing.

pairs.right: every line reviewed as it is typed
nobody skips the checks for being slow

prompt: Which XP value explains most of its testing practices?

choices.text: Courage, to change code nobody wants to touch
choices.why: A value, and not the one behind the testing practices.

choices.text: Simplicity
Respect for the people who write the specification
choices.why: Respect is a value; this wording is not it.

choices.text: Feedback
choices.why: Right: every practice finds out sooner whether something is wrong.

prompt: Tomás reviewed the Wednesday change alone, a day after it was written, and missed the stacking. What did pairing change?

choices.text: Lia found it in testing the same afternoon, before it reached the box office
The question came sooner
choices.why: Right: while the line was being typed, the cheapest moment there is.

choices.text: Tomás stopped reviewing other people’s code
Joana wrote the code herself

prompt: Put XP’s feedback loops in order, from the shortest to the longest.
trap: The inner loops catch slips; the outer ones catch the wrong thing being built.

prompt: How many values does the second edition of Extreme Programming Explained list?
On an XP team, who writes the unit tests?

choices.text: The programmers
choices.why: Right: test first, by the people who write the code.

choices.text: The tester, after the code
The customer
choices.why: The customer writes the acceptance tests, with help.

choices.text: A separate team that runs the automation for the whole company

prompt: What moves towards the tester on an XP team? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: helping the customer write acceptance tests
exploring
pairing with programmers
running the regression suite by hand

prompt: Why did teams find a gap in the first XP books’ arrangement of testing?
hint: Who thinks of the cases nobody mentioned?

choices.text: The unit tests ran too slowly
XP forbade acceptance tests
Customers miss cases, and programmers share their code’s blind spots
choices.why: Right: that gap is the tester’s.

choices.text: There were too many testers

prompt: With continuous integration, a check fails. What does it point at?
hint: How much changed since it last passed?

choices.text: Weeks of work
The tester who wrote the check
Nothing in particular, since checks fail at random
choices.why: A failing check is information about the change.

choices.text: The last change

prompt: The build has been red for three days and the team keeps merging. What has it lost?
hint: Every new failure hides behind the old one.

choices.text: Speed: each merge now takes several hours to finish building
Its pairing
The ability to tell which change broke what
choices.why: Right: a red build is fixed before anything else.

choices.text: Nothing, if the failing check is old
choices.why: Old or not, it hides new failures.

prompt: Hundreds of checks pass every hour. What does green actually say?
hint: Whether the checks say the right thing is another question.

choices.text: The customer is satisfied with how the feature behaves at the box office
There are no defects left in the code that changed
The code does what the checks say
choices.why: Right: not that the checks are right or complete.

choices.text: The software works
choices.why: That is the reading the lesson warns against.

prompt: What does SAFe describe that Scrum, Kanban and XP do not?

choices.text: A single team’s two-week sprint and the events inside it
Many teams on one product
choices.why: Right: the other three describe one team.

choices.text: How to write unit tests
A board with columns

prompt: A Planning Interval has four two-week iterations followed by a two-week innovation and planning iteration. How many weeks long is it?
The price team changes how a discount is stored; the box office terminals read the old format. Both teams’ checks pass. Where does SAFe expect this to be caught?

choices.text: In the retrospective
In the System Team’s end-to-end checks and the System Demo
choices.why: Right: testing no single team owns.

choices.text: In each team’s unit tests
choices.why: They pass, which is the problem.

choices.text: At the next release, when the box office terminals are updated across the chain

prompt: A train uses the innovation and planning iteration to test and fix everything not finished. What is that called, and why is it a trap?

choices.text: A hardening sprint: the waterfall’s testing phase again
choices.why: Right: with the same cost curve.

choices.text: A System Demo, and it is not a trap
PI Planning
choices.why: That is the planning event at the start.

choices.text: Built-in quality

prompt: What question does a tester bring to PI Planning that nobody inside one team would ask?

choices.text: Who is the Scrum Master?
Can the System Team test everything for us at the end?
choices.why: That is the trap, not the question.

choices.text: Which other team reads the data we are changing?
choices.why: Right: the combination question, at scale.

choices.text: How many unit tests will we write?

prompt: Match each way of working to its typical failure.
hint: The last row of the table.

pairs.right: a queue in front of testing

prompt: Where is quality held in Kanban?
hint: Written at the top of each column.

choices.text: The System Team, which owns the end-to-end checks across all the teams
The pair
The policy on each column
The definition of done, written once for the team
choices.why: That is Scrum’s answer, though the policies are close to it.

prompt: Which parts of the job stay the same in every way of working, by this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: prevention first
examples as the base
defects as evidence about the process
a testing phase at the end
choices.why: No: that is the failure each one slides into.

prompt: How did Cine Aurora arrive at its mix of sprints, a Kanban board and XP practices?

choices.text: The Scrum Guide requires a board and pairing alongside sprints
choices.why: It requires nothing of the kind.

choices.text: By fixing one problem at a time
choices.why: Right: which is how most teams end up with theirs.

choices.text: A consultant chose it
By adopting SAFe first and removing the parts it did not need
